correctness.rationale: The exact cross Gram formula F(ts)=(zeta(2)-Li_2(ts))/(1-ts), the first-order dilogarithm expansion, and Frullani integral independently yield the same positive squared Hilbert–Schmidt limit. Step-function kernels converge almost everywhere and have matching L2 norms, so strong L2 and thus S2 convergence follows. Mirsky/Hoffman–Wielandt singular-value inequality yields full l2 list convergence; uniform Hardy norm and domination give the claimed strong C1 limit. 288 exact-rational finite Gram identities and additional numerical normalization tests passed.

value.rationale: The result identifies an explicit continuum Hilbert–Schmidt operator and proves all singular values converge in l2 across a natural compact-to-noncompact transition, beyond an isolated norm calculation. A sharp positive scale-invariant log-cosh metric quantifies why two strongly convergent paths are not close in the Hilbert–Schmidt ideal. This addresses intrinsic spectral geometry of the original generalized Cesàro family and invites subsequent analysis of the new limit operator.
